_about: The dashboard To-Do feed. Refreshed at every Rule 8 checkpoint alongside the session handoff — this is the handoff distilled into plain language for the 📋 button on every tab. Split For Sam (curation / decisions only a human makes) and For Fable (engineering, the next session picks up).
_as_of: 2026-08-27 (SkyPin) · The biggest slice of the implementation money — the Access priority, a third of the pool — turned out to be scored against the wrong number, so every one of the 115 colleges was showing zero earned on it. Not because they had done nothing: the model was reading students who already had credit on a transcript (25 units, three colleges) instead of credit APPLIED for students who came in through the portal or a college landing page, which is what the metric actually asks for. Sam supplied the missing piece — the Potential Student flag is the temporary marker for exactly that group. Fixed and live: 52 colleges now have a real number and 12 are earning. A priority can now be told which data to use instead of the model guessing from the wording, and an unrecognised setting pays nothing loudly rather than paying everything quietly.
_status: The noncredit lane is one decision away from being built. Sam has chosen how it should look on the college table (a second row per college, under the credit row) and how it should be measured, but not how the money splits across its three priorities. Everything else is merged and live. The noncredit figures will read zero until MAP delivers the field that identifies a noncredit location — that is expected, and the page says "no feed" rather than pretending it is a measurement.

items.text: The Title 5 55050 package is ready to send: v5 of the Word file, with every one of your decisions in it and real tracked changes against the version the Board of Governors adopted, plus a Regulatory Action Proposal in the same format as your November one. Undoing every tracked change gives back the adopted regulation word for word, checked by machine. The only blank left is the 2026-27 calendar — five steps to set dates against: the curriculum committee, field vetting, Consultation Council, and two Board readings.

One judgment call left on the package: whether the four policy items from your November draft travel with it or separately. Recommendation is separately — they were argued last November and lost, and bundling lets a reader treat the whole filing as reopening a settled negotiation. Two notes: the new grading clause needs its companion amendment to section 55023, which is what makes a 'credit' mark exist at all; and the no-fee item just gained a second legal anchor, because the Career Passport statute says a student's records must be available at no or low cost.

Three quick fixes on the policy register, now that the draft is settled. Entry #16 points at the wrong lettered paragraph — the August adoption moved that clause. Entry #2 still asks the Legislature for reciprocity between colleges, which is already law; what survives is the 'no second review' half and the CSU/UC half. And entry #10 deserves a fresh look now that #9 is settled: recording the credit was never the same request as flagging where it came from.

The bigger one when you have time. Entry #7 — getting prior-learning credit to generate funding — names the Department of Finance and the attendance rules as its obstacle. A section of the same new bill sets up a workgroup that must design exactly that kind of non-seat-time funding measure and report it to Finance by October 2028. It is scoped to competency-based education rather than prior learning, so it is a venue rather than a solution, but it is the room where this gets designed and we are not in it yet.

Separate from the regulation and probably bigger. The new law makes every dollar of implementation funding conditional on 'the metrics described in paragraph (1)' — and paragraph (1) describes four goals and supplies no metrics at all. Somebody has to define them, and the Implementation Funding model is the only college-by-college quantification of those goals that exists. It already covers access and completion, and the pilot-project one is satisfied because MAP is named in the statute. Career advancement is the gap you said you would cover through CPL Projects and the Credential Registry. This needs no rulemaking, which is exactly its advantage — keep it out of the amendment conversation.

The memory entries are now readable end to end in plain English — 202 were rewritten, and there are no entries left without plain text, none with developer jargon, and no British spellings. The hopper of unreviewed entries is worth an afternoon whenever you have one. Two small things still need you: one entry is marked stale but still carries a verification stamp, which needs your go to clear, and 26 verified entries do not name who verified them.

Sierra ran out of API credit this evening and you restored it — thank you. That is the third time (21 Aug, 22 Aug, 25 Aug). The uptime monitor did its job and raised the alert, but it only looks every three hours, so an outage can run that long before anyone is told. A balance-threshold alert on the Anthropic account itself would catch it before it becomes an outage, and that is the one thing a monitor here cannot do.

Sierra is running on Haiku 4.5 as the temporary cost measure you asked for — about a third the price of what it was on (Sonnet, not Opus). When corporate billing is released, switching back needs no code change and no session: set CPL_CHAT_MODEL on the Supabase project to claude-sonnet-4-6. Worth trying the whole-register sweep on Haiku once before you rely on it — a sixteen-row legal analysis is the hardest thing the assistant does, and it is where a smaller model would show first.

Settled, and noted so nobody undoes it: the automated check found 40 of 41 answers still correct on Haiku, and the one it dropped was the caveat beside the big waiting-credit number — the reminder that roughly a third of reviewed credit is correctly ruled Not Applicable, so the total is a ceiling rather than a debt. You said you can live with it for now, so it stays as it is. The fix is written down and ready if you change your mind: move that caveat next to the number itself instead of into a rules list further away, which would make it stick on any model.

for_sam.title: Decide how noncredit's money splits across its three priorities
for_sam.note: THE ONE THING BLOCKING THE BUILD. The credit side splits 34/33/33 between Access, Outreach and Success. Noncredit can inherit those, which keeps it to one number to change later, or have its own. Nothing has been decided and everything else for the noncredit lane is ready.

for_sam.title: Decide the noncredit minimum award
for_sam.note: Still open. At $50,000, 30 of the 33 noncredit institutions sit exactly on the minimum and growth does not start paying until 3,909 FTES — the opposite of the incentive you wanted. At $15,000 nobody is on the minimum and growth pays from 384 FTES. $60,000 is not affordable at all.

for_sam.title: Move the noncredit line out of the credit priority's strategy list
for_sam.note: Year-1 Access still lists "noncredit mirror courses" among the things a college can do to earn credit-side money. Harmless today, but it belongs to the noncredit lane the moment that lane goes live. One line.

for_sam.title: ITPI: can a college have its own noncredit landing page?
for_sam.note: Only ITPI can answer. MAP is adding a field naming which noncredit location a student came from. Whether an ordinary college can have a second, noncredit landing page — or only the standalone institutions like NOCE and SDCCE — decides whether this covers about 108 colleges or a handful.

for_sam.title: Look at the Fact Sheet and Sierra pages on your phone
for_sam.note: Both were reworked for small screens and checked by measurement, but nobody has actually held them in a hand. Carried from the last two sessions.

for_sam.title: One memory entry carries a stamp that is not true
for_sam.note: It is marked as checked by a curator while also being marked out of date. Needs your call on which it is. The eleven entries credited to you and Jenni are real attribution and should never be swept.

for_fable.title: Build the noncredit lane earning, and its row on the college table
for_fable.note: Waiting only on Sam's split above. The measures are already declared and deliberately empty, so they will read "no feed" until MAP delivers the location field and then start working with no further change. The row shape is decided: a second row per college under the credit row, with short CR and NC labels.

for_fable.title: An alarm for when a scheduled job silently does not run
for_fable.note: Still not built. A dropped run leaves nothing behind — no failure, nothing queued — so silence and success look identical. It has to be attached to a job that still runs, work out what is overdue from the schedules themselves rather than a list someone maintains, and only complain when every attempt in a day is missed.

for_fable.title: Write down the real fix for the repeated 'unpushed commits' warning
for_fable.note: The warning after a merge is caused by a leftover local pointer to the branch GitHub deleted. One command clears it for good. The troubleshooting notes currently say only to confirm it and ignore it, which means every session re-diagnoses it.

for_fable.title: The sign-in email button does not respond to a click
for_fable.note: Reported by Sam, not yet fixed. Clicking fails while tabbing to it works, which points at the field being rebuilt underneath the pointer.

for_fable.note: Reported by Sam, not yet fixed.
